critical_code_review_comments: AuthCallback.jsx now uses a useRef hasProcessed guard set synchronously before the async /auth/session POST; this matches the Emergent OAuth playbook guidance for React.StrictMode one-time exchanges.
AuthCallback.jsx clears window.location.hash via history.replaceState immediately after reading session_id, before the async exchange resolves.
AppRouter reads useLocation().hash and AuthContext skips /auth/me when session_id is present, which avoids callback/auth-check races.

rca_of_the_issue: Previous failure was React.StrictMode re-running the AuthCallback effect and posting the one-time OAuth session_id twice. The current code prevents that by setting hasProcessed.current = true before any async work and stripping the hash immediately after reading session_id. Runtime evidence showed one POST only. The /api/auth/session response was MOCKED because no real Google/Emergent one-time session_id was available.
